doc.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Worries about the future of jazz and Disney World work
summary: He takes things year by year and fears needing a Disney World job.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: What do you envision down the road. Do you think ten years ahead for yourself, and the future of this music?

Well as I said before, Monk, I’m a little concerned about the future of this music and I try not to think about ten years down the road. I try to look at things year by year. If the phone keeps ringing I’m in good shape. And so far, so good. But what happens, in ten

years, gee I don’t really know. I am concerned about it. I live in the Orlando area so I worked at Walt Disney World some, sub out there with other bands and stuff like that. What concerns me is I envision myself ending up having to try to get a regular job at Walt Disney World because I can’t make a living any other way. Hopefully not.
